text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan's special envoy on Afghanistan Iftikhar Murshed will visit Tehran next week to meet Iran's new Foreign Minister Kamal Khirzdi.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will visit Moscow in March, 1998 and consultations are being held to finalise the dates.
- Pakistan and Romania will discuss a multi-billion dollar investment plan when the joint ministerial commission of the two countries meets in Islamabad on August 5.
- The government plans to convene a session of parliament on August 14 to mark Pakistan's golden jubilee celeberations.
- The Privatisation Commission has decided to privatise a substantial chunk of state-owned corporations through stock markets to get better prices.
- Visiting Indian businessmen's team leader Binay Kumar has called for promotion of trade between India and Pakistan.
- The Punjab provincial government appears to have agreed to hold a dialogue with some farmers' organisations to defuse the current unrest against the agriculture tax.
- Board of Investment Chairman Humayun Akhtar says a new investment policy is under formulation which will provide special incentives to foreign business houses.
- Minister of State for Water and Power Haleem Siddiqui says the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation loses 2.5 billion rupees annualy owing to power theft.

- The government has assured the International Monetary Fund to privatise major public sector enterprises within this year to generate essentially required funds for clearance of its short-term foreign debts.
